tagline: The freeway that never came, built as a parkway instead.
intro: From PA 63 in Montgomery Township, US 202 runs as a parkway, landscaped and lined with split-rail fence, with a walking and cycling trail alongside. It is four lanes as far as PA 463, then narrows to two and winds northeast through woods and fields into Bucks County, crossing Neshaminy Creek before it meets the PA 611 freeway at Doylestown. Billboards are banned along the way.

It was a long time coming. After decades of failed freeway plans, it became a parkway when funding was cut in 2005, and opened in December 2012. Businesses on the old route lost customers, and in 2015 they won a Business 202 designation in hopes of getting them back.

moments.title: PA 309 interchange, Montgomeryville
moments.text: South of Montgomeryville the parkway trail slips under the road, then loops back to cross over PA 309 on the same bridge as the traffic.

moments.title: Neshaminy Creek
moments.text: In Doylestown Township the road crosses the creek on the 1st Lt. Travis L. Manion Memorial Bridge and runs on through a mix of fields and woods.
